**Real size and free space.** An unlocked drive now shows the size and free
space of the disk it lives on, instead of a made-up 1 TB with 512 GB free.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.3.1-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.3.1-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again).

## Fixed

- **Drive size and free space** in Explorer and Finder are now those of the
  disk the drive's folder is on. Nothing is reserved for a drive: its files
  are ordinary files in that folder, so it grows as you add to it and shares
  the disk's free space with everything else there. A drive kept on C: shows
  C:'s size and free space.
- On Windows the free space shown updates whenever something is written to
  the drive; space used on the same disk by other programs shows up then, or
  when the drive is next unlocked.

## Known limitations

- **The macOS app has not yet been tested on a real Mac.** Treat it as a
  preview and keep a backup of anything you put in a drive.
- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
